about: READ-ONLY: renders what `github-disable-actions` WOULD set on a GitHub repository, and changes nothing (infra/forge/github-act.sh disable-actions --plan; backlog e727fcfd). It reads, as the GitHub App's installation on <owner>, the repository (refusing one that is archived, moved, a fork or invisible) and its Actions permission, GET /repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/permissions, and renders the state — Actions enabled true or false — and the act: PUT {"enabled":false}, or none when Actions already read disabled. Run on algedonic-dev boss-dr it machine-reads the setting David made by hand on 2026-09-29: act none means it holds. An answer without a boolean enabled, or an unusable token slot, is a failure or a refusal, not a plan. No clock and no token in the bytes; its sha256 is printed on stderr as `plan-sha256:`, and that hash is what David's passkey signs (design 17835005 q1).
